title: Cel-Shaded models with Claude opus 5.5
author: DarthInMyPants
selftext:
Hey there everyone I wanted to see some examples of cel-shaded 3d models that people have generated using Claude opus 5.5

I’m working on a big project that’ll eventually need cel shaded character models in an anime style, so I’m trying to grasp how that looks and works for everyone else.

comments.author: DarthInMyPants
comments.body: And ofc I’ve been using the blender mcp server to create temporary models so I already know about that.

comments.author: Recoil42
comments.body:
>I’m working on a big project that’ll eventually need cel shaded character models in an anime style, so I’m trying to grasp how that looks 

Ask Opus to generate cel-shaded character models for you to grasp how that looks. If you don't like how that looks, ask Opus to change it.

replies.author: DarthInMyPants
replies.body: I’m not wanting to use my usage up, I’ve already used up 65% of my weekly in 2 days (I’m getting better at managing it, didn’t know I had to open new chats and /compact often)

replies.author: Recoil42
replies.body:
>I’m getting better at managing it, didn’t know I had to open new chats and /compact often

You don't have to do either of those things and really *should not* do either of those things in most cases.

replies.author: DarthInMyPants
replies.body: Why not? It’s worked for me so far to keep usage down

replies.author: Recoil42
replies.body: It definitely hasn't. Compaction resets your cache. Whoever gave you that advice is feeding you a load.

replies.author: Recoil42
replies.body: Generally, you should let Claude Code compact automatically and when it decides compaction is necessary.

replies.author: Viese93
replies.body: Claude told me itself to open new chats within a project to keep usage down otherwise it reads the entire chat each new entry

replies.author: Recoil42
replies.body:
That isn't really true as long as you're heads-down doing continuous work. Context is cached, all you 'pay' for is new messages. Look up KV caching.

Things only work differently if you're away from the computer for extended periods of time.

comments.author: Cubey42
comments.body: I'm gonna be so real, unless you use tripo to help and want to do a lot of tedious cleanup/iteration, we just aren't there yet for models. Doesn't mean you couldn't get started on the design of the game first anyway. Characters and details mean nothing if the game isn't fun to play, and you can easily test the design by using placeholders in the meantime

replies.author: CycleMother2006
replies.body:
Claude can do basic props if we're talking cel-shaded. Most cel-shaded stuff is composed heavily of basic primitive shapes with some simple modifiers. You can easily do light posts, dumpsters, fire hydrants, traffic signs, etc.

It's different when we're talking realistic props at high detail, but with cel-shaded  99% of the detail is carried by the shader, lighting, and color choices. 

That said, I would not have claude or any other LLM touch character models. Tripo or Meshy 100% on that front. Or you can use a CC0 (such as one of Blender's community models) or a character creator like Reallusion (though the company's licensing is toxic as hell), metahuman, or something else. Though if not building on Unreal metahuman is probably too high poly and can be significant work to get stylized characters working.

comments.author: CraftyWitchInc
comments.body: My game uses the cel-shaded style using screenshots of games that also used that style, and opus 5.5 did really well with environmental objects, not the best with human or animal models. For those I recommend using CC0 base models that are the closest to what you want and then have them painted or modified however you want. Just prepare to either give a lot of references or do a lot of reiterating.
